claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure exhibiting multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A microstructure-aware, physics-constrained machine-learning framework will accurately predict Young’s modulus.
A microstructure-aware, physics-constrained machine-learning framework will accurately predict yield strength.
A microstructure-aware, physics-constrained machine-learning framework will accurately predict fracture toughness.
The proposed framework will be more accurate than traditional prediction methods.
The proposed framework will provide a 10–100× computational speedup over traditional methods.
High-resolution TEM or EBSD descriptors can capture the local chemical and structural fluctuations relevant to the alloy.
Localized microstructural heterogeneities govern the alloy’s mechanical response.
Physics constraints will prevent nonphysical model predictions.
Using a surrogate model will reduce reliance on computationally intensive first-principles and CALPHAD simulations.
Young’s modulus predictions will be within ±10–15% of experimental measurements.
Yield-strength predictions will be within ±10–15% of experimental measurements.
Fracture-toughness predictions will be within ±10–15% of experimental measurements.
Thermophysical-parameter calculations, CALPHAD, and first-principles methods are more computationally intensive than the proposed framework.
Existing traditional methods have lower predictive accuracy for fracture toughness.
The method may become unreliable when imaging resolution is insufficient to represent critical local heterogeneities.
Unexpected phase transformations or structural evolution outside the training domain may make the method unreliable.
Extreme temperatures or strain rates not represented by the physics constraints may make the method unreliable.
Related hybrid approaches have demonstrated a 10–20% improvement in prediction accuracy.
Related hybrid approaches have demonstrated an order-of-magnitude computational advantage.
